name: MO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Wesley Bell running with large financial advantage
model.rationale: The baseline of D+28.8 rests on a heavily Democratic St. Louis-area seat, an incumbent with $3.6M raised, and markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty; no evidence justifies moving away from it.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Bell underperforming in low-turnout conditions could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 1st District, centered on St. Louis, is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+29. Incumbent Wesley Bell, first elected in 2024 after unseating longtime incumbent Cori Bush in the primary, is running for reelection with a substantial war chest of over $3.5 million raised and more than $1 million on hand. His Republican opponent, Paul Berry, reports no fundraising, and outside spending overwhelmingly favors Bell.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert ratings for this race, so the forecast relies on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which point the same direction. Prediction markets give Bell roughly a 98% chance of winning. The expected margin is about 29 points, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating.
